articles.title: West Ham cut loose to hit Wrexham for six and go top of Championship
articles.summary: West Ham secured their fourth league win in a row as they returned to the top of the Championship with a thumping 6-0 win over Wrexham at the London Stadium. It was a marvellous display of attacking football from Nuno Espírito Santo’s side, who swept to victory with room to spare and with six…
body: Jarrod Bowen got the ball rolling after 28 minutes, Joël Piroe made it two before the break, then Konstantinos Mavropanos, Taty Castellanos, Mohamadou Kanté and Manor Solomon all scored in the second half as the Welsh side were dealt a hiding. The performance was further evidence the Hammers are finding their feet in the second tier after failing to win any of their first three games following Premier League relegation.

They should have led inside seven minutes, Castellanos sending a free header from Solomon’s cross over from six yards. Bowen then got clear in the box from a quick throw, but his shot was turned against the crossbar by a reflex save from Anthony Patterson. From the corner that resulted, Mavropanos headed a foot wide at the far post.

Piroe was guilty of an awful miss midway through the half, leaning back and blasting high into the Wrexham fans behind Patterson’s goal. Bowen showed him how it was done a minute later. Morato’s cross from the right was timed perfectly into the six-yard box, where the home side’s captain was arriving ahead of Jacques Ekomié to guide it into the far corner.

articles.title: Like Benzema & as good as Haaland - Alonso on Joao Pedro
articles.summary: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso says striker Joao Pedro is similar stylistically to his former Real Madrid team-mate Karim Benzema and is at a comparable level to Manchester City's Erling Haaland.
body: Xabi Alonso says Chelsea striker Joao Pedro is similar in style to his former Real Madrid team-mate Karim Benzema - and at a comparable level to Manchester City 's Erling Haaland.
The Brazil international, 24, has scored twice and provided two assists in his first three games of the season - and was named the Premier League's Player of the Month on Friday.
It was the first time Joao Pedro has won the award as he finished ahead of team-mate Cole Palmer, who was Chelsea 's previous recipient in September 2024.
When asked whether the forward could be compared to the prolific Haaland, who won last season's Premier League Golden Boot with 27 goals, Blues boss Alonso said: "I would say yes.

articles.title: Jakob Ingebrigtsen blows away bitter rival Hocker in Ultimate Championships 5,000m
articles.summary: Norwegian leaves rival Hocker trailing to claim $150,000. Briton Jazmin Sawyers second in the women’s long jump. It is a scene that has become gloriously familiar down the years.
body: The sweetness? That came from winning a mammoth first prize of $150,000 after an achilles injury he feared might derail his career. And the spice? Well, that was provided by the way Ingebrigtsen utterly obliterated his great American rival Cole Hocker, a man he had branded a “coward” just a week ago.

Ingebrigtsen has never been shy of venturing an opinion, and he was aggrieved when Hocker insisted on having his own pacemaker for the 1500m Diamond League final – and then refused to follow him. That led to a high-publicised war of words, and a rematch that was the talk of Budapest.

And, my, did it live up to the hype. The pace was quick, but the Norwegian was so confident he had time to look around twice on the final lap before launching a devastating final kick to win in 12min 59.24sec, with Hocker, the reigning 5,000m world champion, nearly a second back.
“I was predicted number 12 by World Athletics can you imagine?” said a bemused Ingebrigtsen, who is the Olympic champion at this distance after all.

articles.title: ‘A perfect storm’: Trescothick refuses to blame England bowlers after Razaullah’s onslaught
articles.summary: Pakistan’s ninth-wicket pair put on 121 in 123 balls. ‘You’ve got to give a bit more credit to them’ Marcus Trescothick described Pakistan’s late-innings onslaught as a “perfect storm”, after the 21-year-old debutant Razaullah and the 36-year-old Mohammad Abbas combined to score 121 off 123 balls…
body: The interim coach refused to characterise England’s frequently puzzling efforts in the field as embarrassing as Razaullah plundered nine sixes and four fours on his way to a score of 81, and Abbas two sixes – as many as he had scored in 46 career Test innings before the start of this series – in his 42, insisting: “You’ve got to give a bit more credit to them [rather] than trying to target everything that we’ve tried to do.”
Trescothick added: “You’d always like to think that you can do it better, and you analyse it afterwards and say, was there an error, or was there a tactic we missed?

“You just hope in those situations when you bowl in the right place, which we did on many occasions, that you get the nick, or you bowl them … We hoped to go through them pretty quickly, but they kept smacking it and the young fella came in and made it tricky because when he hit it, he hit it a long way.”
Trescothick praised the all-round performance of Razaullah, who has been a revelation with bat and ball in a much-changed Pakistan side.

articles.title: Wigan beat Catalans to lift sixth League Leaders' Shield
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors win a sixth League Leaders' Shield as they beat Catalans Dragons to wrap up top spot in Super League heading into the play-offs.
body: Wigan Warriors won a sixth League Leaders' Shield as they ran in nine tries to beat Catalans Dragons and carry on their remarkable run of form heading into the Super League play-offs.

Matt Peet's side, who were trophyless in 2025 off the back of their quadruple-winning 2024 campaign, have now won two pieces of silverware, having lifted the Challenge Cup in May, and are now two games away from a treble.
Harry Smith and Ugo Tison exchanged tries early on, but Liam Marshall, Brad O'Neill and Liam Farrell put Wigan in control at the break.

Austin Daniel and Jai Field continued Wigan's scoring streak, while Zach Eckersley, Adam Keighran and Marshall's second wrapped up a thumping 16th win in a row, with Alexis Lis scoring a fine consolation try for Les Dracs in the closing stages.

articles.title: 'Out of control' - Cook questions England tactics
articles.summary: England had “no plan” and were “out of control” in the face of Razaullah’s stunning hitting on the third day of the final Test against Pakistan, according to former captain Alastair Cook.
body: Razaullah, the 21-year-old batting at number nine on Test debut, clobbered 81 from 63 balls at Edgbaston.
He shared a ninth-wicket partnership of 121 with Muhammad Abbas to drag the third Test into an unlikely fourth day, with England set 130 for victory.
Though the hosts are heavy favourites to earn a 3-0 clean sweep, the carnage of the final session was an alarming spell as Joe Root begins his second spell as captain.
Root's tactics were often criticised in his first spell as skipper and there were further questions of the Yorkshireman when he stood in for former captain Ben Stokes earlier this summer.

articles.summary: Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé has this week revealed his appreciation for the talents of Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal. Attackers Mbappé and Lamine have of course continued to dominate the headlines across world football over recent days.
body: Not only that, but the pair featured front and centre on the 30-man shortlist for the 2026 Ballon d’Or, considered as being amongst the very favourites to lift the coveted prize.
And as alluded to above, this week, Mbappé has admitted that he is a keen admirer of the talents of the Spanish World Cup winner.
“Which players excite me right now? I don’t want to name names because if I forget someone… To say who the ten or fifteen best players in the world are, I think everyone would agree.

”I also like Estevão; he has a special creativity. Here, Arda Güler can go very far. Endrick has potential; he’s a goalscorer. Warren (Zaïre-Emery) and Désiré (Doué) are going to have great careers, for sure.”

articles.title: Hunt sets sights on Lions tour after injury return
articles.summary: England scrum-half Natasha Hunt says the inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour to New Zealand - the first Test of which is exactly a year away today - is a massive motivation as she prepares to make her comeback from injury.
body: The 37-year-old sustained knee ligament damage during England's Six Nations opener against Ireland in April.

She was sidelined for the rest of the Red Roses' Grand-Slam winning campaign and Gloucester-Hartpury's run to the PWR semi-finals, but starts at nine in England's WXV Global Series opener against Australia in Salford on Saturday.
"I've been fortunate enough to have played in Team GB Sevens set-ups twice over," said Hunt, a veteran of the Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2021 Olympics.
"That was some of my favourite, most enjoyable rugby, just mixing cultures, everyone having a common goal and coming together really quickly to try to get something special done.

articles.title: Wigan storm to Super League's League Leaders' Shield and remain on treble course
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors clinched Super League's top spot and the League Leaders' Shield after a final-round 50-12 victory over Catalans Dragons, meaning Matt Peet's side remain on course for a domestic treble.
body: Having clinched Challenge Cup glory in May at Wembley with victory over Hull KR, Wigan lifted their second piece of silverware on Friday via a dominant home win over the Dragons.

Warriors scored nine tries through Harry Smith, Liam Marshall (two), Brad O'Neill, the retiring Liam Farrell, Austin Daniel, Jai Field, Zach Eckersley and Adam Keighran. Keighran also added 14 points off the kicking tee.

The only other side capable of claiming top spot and the League Leaders' Shield had been Leeds Rhinos, and owing to their far greater points difference, a victory over Hull FC would have been enough had Wigan slipped up, but Peet's side ensured that was never likely to happen. In any case, Leeds fell to a shock 18-12 home defeat to Hull on Friday.

Wigan will now seek to finish their season by clinching a treble with Super League Grand Final success at Old Trafford on October 3, having suffered final defeat last season to Hull KR. They and Leeds will have next week off as the play-offs begin, before contesting respective semi-finals at home on September 25 and 26.

articles.title: Taylor Townsend and Katerina Siniakova complete career grand slam together with US Open doubles title
articles.summary: The top seed fought back from a set down to beat wildcards Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery 5-7 6-0 6-2 on Arthur Ashe Stadium. Victory for the pair followed triumph at Wimbledon in 2024, the Australian Open in 2025 and the French Open earlier this year.
body: Taylor Townsend and Katerina Siniakova completed the career grand slam together as they won their first US Open women’s doubles title as a pairing on Friday.

It was a fourth major title for American Townsend and a 12th in doubles for Czech Siniakova, who made history as the first player to complete the career grand slam with two different partners, after she previously did so with compatriot Barbora Krejcikova.
The 2025 runners-up conceded the first set as Siniakova hit three double faults in the final game - the first set they had dropped all tournament.
But the top seeds roared back in the second, winning 23 of 27 points after the first game to force a deciding set, which they also dominated.

articles.summary: Former Pakistan captain Urooj Mumtaz lauded youngster Razaullah and said he wrote the "perfect chapter" to revive his reeling side after his sensational 81 off 63 balls against England on day three at Edgbaston.
body: Razaullah, who has only played eight previous first-class matches in his career, smacked nine sixes in his remarkable innings, equalling Tim Southee's record for the most maximums for a Test debutant, dazzling in a 121-run partnership with Mohammad Abbas (42) that eventually propelled Pakistan to a total of 449 and set England a target of 130.
The 21-year-old consolidated an already impressive performance on debut with the ball, taking four wickets in England's innings, including that of skipper Joe Root for his first.

His performance with the bat was undoubtedly the deciding factor in forcing the match into a fourth day that looked so improbable when he arrived at the crease, when Pakistan trailed by two runs at 318-8.
"His innings was simply sensational," Mumtaz said on Sky Sports. "A perfectly written first chapter of his Test career. All that passion, the flair of Pakistan cricket!

articles.title: Will it be a Sabalenka 'three-peat' or maiden US Open for new No 1 Rybakina?
articles.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka is looking to become the first woman to achieve the 'three-peat' in New York since Serena Williams in 2014 but she faces incoming world No 1 Elena Rybakina in the US Open final on Saturday.
body: Rybakina's results this year, starting with her Australian Open final triumph against Sabalenka, will see her rise to the top of the rankings on Monday, ending the Belarussian's 99-week reign.

But Sabalenka can exact some revenge for both that defeat and being overtaken at the WTA summit by defending her US Open title against Rybakina in Saturday's Flushing Meadows final - live on Sky Sports Tennis from 5pm.
"I really understand about how tough it is to reach the world No 1," said Sabalenka.
"It's a lot of work and, yeah, that was one of my goals, but right now there was not much I could do. I didn't really perform well in the middle of the season.
